subject: BrightByte renewal forecast checkpoint — Q3 commit + churn triage
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@brightbyte.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: BrightByte renewal planning & initial numbers

Hi Mina / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're starting to pull together our internal renewal plan for the July 31 renewal and wanted to share the preliminary numbers and a few risk flags so you can bake them into the forecast. High-level:

- Contract ARR rolling to renew: $1.12M
- Renewal ask: 12-month renewal at current seat tiers (they may down-tier 10% of usage for one product)
- Primary internal risk: billing timing + procurement review (legal needs a final SOW)

I've attached the spreadsheet with our internal scenario lines (sheet: "BB_scenarios_v1"). The three things we'd like from Redwood for the forecasting window:
1) Confirm whether the current committed seat baseline (as of 6/30) is eligible for a straight renew or whether we need a formal reprovision step that could delay billing into Aug.
2) Any early indicators from your side on support tickets or escalations that correlate with churn risk.
3) A short timeslot this week for a quick alignment sync — 30 minutes.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a call if it's faster.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Finance, BrightByte
liam.o@brightbyte.io

Attachment: BrightByte_MA_Plan.pdf (PDF, 214 KB)

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@brightbyte.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-01T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte renewal planning & initial numbers

Liam — thanks for the details and the plan. Quick notes from our side and next steps:

- Committed baseline: We can confirm that seats active as of 2028-06-30 are eligible for standard renewal routing. There is no reprovision requirement unless the customer requests a contract restructure. That means, for forecasting, treat current committed ARR as eligible for renewal billing in July unless procurement requests hold.

- Billing timing risk: If BrightByte's procurement requires a signed SOW + PO before invoice generation, there is a likely slip into early August. Can you confirm expected PO ETA?

- Support/escalation indicators: Ben, can you pull the last 90-day support ticket volume for BrightByte (severity 1/2) and any open escalations to include as a churn-risk multiplier?

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to add ticket volume and health score into the attached renewal model (BB_renewal_model_v3.xlsx).
2) Jordan to run a quick forecast sensitivity that shows revenue if 0%, 10%, and 20% downgrade occurs.
3) Mina to host a 30-min alignment tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT (invite to follow) to lock commit probability for the Finance forecast.

If PO ETA is > 7 days, we recommend marking the deal as 60% commit for this week's forecast and tagging as "procurement timing" risk.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: BB_renewal_model_v3.xlsx (Excel, 38 KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Liam O'Connor <liam.o@brightbyte.io>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte renewal planning & initial numbers

Adding the support/health inputs here — pulled the last 90 days:

- Total tickets: 16 (3 Sev2, 0 Sev1)
- Open escalations: 1 (performance regression on model inference p95 in EU region)
- CS health score (last quarterly): 7/10

I've updated BB_renewal_model_v3.xlsx with a Support_Risk multiplier and a column with adjusted probabilities. Short summary:
- Baseline (no downgrade): 82% commit probability -> $918k expected in July
- 10% downgrade scenario: 68% commit probability -> $760k expected
- Procurement delay (PO >7 days): immediate billing shifts to Aug; mark as "billing slip" in forecast.

Mina — I put hypothetical tickets -> churn impact mapping in the sheet. Liam — if the procurement route requires a revised SOW, that becomes the gating item for us to move to an invoice. If you can share expected legal review window, we can mark the timing more precisely.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Ops, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: BB_renewal_model_v3.xlsx (updated), notes in sheet 'Support_Risk'

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@brightbyte.io>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte renewal planning & initial numbers — Forecast action

Thanks everyone — short directive for Finance forecast intake:

- Mark the BrightByte deal (RB-2028-BB-1423) as Commit = 70% for the week close given Procurement uncertainty and the open performance escalation. This reflects Ben's updated support risk and Mina's procurement timing note.
- Create two line items in the weekly forecast: 1) July recognized ARR (70% commit if PO cleared by 7/31), 2) Contingent Aug recognition (30% of deal tagged as billing_slip).
- Mina: confirm PO ETA in the sync tomorrow and flag any legal/SOW changes immediately to finance@redwood.com.

I'll update the forecast spreadsheet with the two-line entry and reference the Drive model. If the PO arrives and legal signoff is complete by 7/25, we can move the contingent line back into July.

Appreciate the fast turn — please keep thread updates to quick single-line statuses after the sync.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
